display.title: Shlomo HaMelech's Pool, Part 2
display.summary_short: Hidden in a doctor's home, Rabbi Yehuda goes fishing for Shabbos, and a lost royal ring and a clever plan save the Jews from a cruel decree.
display.summary_long: Rabbi Yehuda, rescued from the river, is still hiding in the home of the kind Jewish doctor Rabbi Yitzchak. After many months the doctor takes him fishing at night for Shabbos, and soon Rabbi Yehuda goes every Thursday by himself. One hot summer night the king, out for a walk by the river, loses his royal ring in the water, and no one can find it. The wicked advisor Ivan has the king decree that the Jews must find the ring within 30 days or be expelled. The Rav calls the community to fast, daven and say Tehillim. On the 25th day Rabbi Yehuda brings home a fish with the king's ring inside. Rabbi Yitzchak keeps the find a secret and works out a plan. On the 30th day, as the whole community gathers by the river, a figure in white floats up on a raft, and the plan unfolds that returns Rabbi Yehuda to the palace and ends Ivan's schemes for good. The story is followed by about ten minutes of an unrelated recording of children singing Yiddish and Pesach songs.
display.lesson: Hashem watches over the Jewish people; when a decree threatens, we fast, daven and say Tehillim, and Hashem sends the salvation.

advisories.note: The king decrees that all the Jews will be expelled if they cannot find his lost ring.
At the end the villain is thrown into the river and does not come back.
